citations.field: 女 entry: script-form account, senses and cited examples; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-1100/source.png
citations.text: The entry calls 女 pictographic. It describes oracle-bone forms as a woman kneeling with her hands crossed before her chest, and says some forms add a head stroke interpreted as headwear. It describes the kneeling posture as less apparent in Spring and Autumn bronze forms, with Warring States forms following those bronze forms with changed stroke manner; clerical writing turns the vertical kneeling stroke into a horizontal stroke. It gives the core meaning as female, contrasted with 男, and cites a bronze-inscription example and the transmitted 易 for 女 meaning female. It separately reports 女 read as 母 in an oracle-bone example, as 汝 in bronze inscriptions, and as 如 in Warring States writing. The entry also records a distinct nù reading for ‘give a woman in marriage’, citing 國語. These source-reported uses and citations do not by themselves establish a dated semantic development or the dates of each cited inscription.
